mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding 6 months raises discount rates, reducing present value of future corporate earnings and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) signals weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for three consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both above 12-month moving average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.4%) in at least 50% of triggered quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) above their 6-month moving averages signals a robust demand environment, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both above 6-month moving average
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals labor market strength, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profitability, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS above 12-month moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.6%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) for five consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, regardless of the economic regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 55% of triggered periods.
